title: Decision tree truncation error
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\alpha$ be a type with decidable equality, and let $T$ be a decision tree querying Boolean coordinates among $n$ coordinates and returning values in $\alpha$. For any fallback value $a\in\alpha$ and any real number $\varepsilon>0$, the fraction of inputs in $\{0,1\}^n$ on which $T$ differs from the tree obtained by truncating at depth $\left\lceil\log_2\bigl(L/\varepsilon\bigr)\right\rceil$ and assigning $a$ at each truncation point is at most $\varepsilon$, where $L$ is the number of leaves of $T$.
hypotheses_covered: A nonnegative integer number $n$ of Boolean coordinates
A decision tree $T$ on those coordinates with outputs in $\alpha$
